milestones.rejection_reason: The submitted document is not valid and our automated title verification was unable to locate and match the property to the customer, it shows that the property owner is “RITA K DIETZ” and per SOLRITE's Underwriting Policy, a property owner must be the signatory on the agreement.In order for approval, the customer can submit one of the following documents:A third-party title report.A current mortgage statement not older than two (2) months.Upload a Legal document outlining real property ownership, including Grant Deed, Warranty Deed, or similar legal document, which is recorded with the registry of land records.In the case of a newly closed home sale, closing documentation showing evidence of homeowner name and address is shown.If they are married, the customer can submit the marriage certificate.

As a result, this submittal is rejected at this time.To proceed, please revise the design so that all system specifications are fully aligned with the approved planset, including (but not limited to):- Module quantity and layout per array- Tilt values (degrees)- Azimuth values (degrees)- Any additional electrical or mechanical parameters shown in the plansetOnce the PV design matches the latest planset file, please resubmit for further review. For detailed design and documentation requirements, refer to our submission guidelines at: SUBMISSION – Shade Study – NTP Stage. SUBMISSION - Shade Study - NTP Stage This shade study is rejected because NREL shading was used instead of Google Solar.Please restore the original configuration for the shade study using the Map image source set to either Google Imagery or Nearmap (Nearmap is strongly recommended when there are trees or other nearby obstructions).The solar data source is required to be set back to Google Solar before resubmission.

milestones.label: Building Planset
milestones.rejection_reason: ID: SLRT-AU 001Multiple inconsistencies have been identified in the submitted planset. The following items do not align with the equipment specifications outlined in the signed agreement:D600-M2A x 10The design file currently reflects the following non‑contract items and/or configurations:D600-M2A x 8 and D350-M1A x 4Please revise the design file to match the contracted scope or submit the required change order(s) to proceed with the review process. ID: SLRT-CUSTOM SET-01Customized rejection executed. Please review the following notice:Per OEM, the trunk cable must be 10 AWG. ID: SLRT-DESIGN-ELEC 002NEC Article: 690.9 (125% Rule) Subject: The OCPDs must be rated non less than 125% of the maximum continuos current calculated. Resolution Required:PV OCPD located into the Main PV combiner panel requires an update. The continuous current from the 9 module string is calculated at 14.1 A, but the current OCPD placed in the design is Oversized, please update.

milestones.rejection_reason: Please upload a new shade study that matches the Plan set's specifications (Layout, Azimuth, and Tilt) FYI: If the production resulting from the layout change is outside our production tolerance of -4% & +10% a HCO will be required to justify the new production values.

milestones.label: Building Planset
milestones.rejection_reason: Please verify the equipment specifications. The planset indicates 32 D600 microinverters and 2 D350 microinverters; however, the agreement specifies 30 D600 microinverters and 3 D350 microinverters.Additionally, Port 2 of the PV solar system within the AC hub has a maximum continuous current capacity of 32A. Please confirm the correct equipment configuration and ensure compatibility with the system specifications.

milestones.label: As-Built Planset
milestones.rejection_reason: The plan set specifies a PV module model that differs from the module shown in the installation photos. Please update the plan set to accurately reflect the installed PV module model. The array layout shown in the shade study doesn't match the configuration indicated in the plan set. Please update the shade study to reflect the array design specified in the plan set and verify the resulting production accordingly.Additionally, ensure that all documentation is consistent with the actual installation configuration shown in the site photos.The shade study and plan set indicate four estimated array tilt angles; however, the installation photos only show three array sections, with one of them installed at an approximate tilt angle of 44 degrees, which significantly exceeds the allowable tolerance.Please update both the plan set and the shade study to accurately reflect the as-built installation configuration.The contactor model shown in the installation photos doesn't match the model specified in the SLD. Please update the plan set to accurately reflect the installed equipment configuration.

milestones.label: Install Photo Approval
milestones.rejection_reason: 1.3 - Equipment on wallInclude the Main Service panel, monitoring equipment, disconnects, conduit, Preferably, please once the entire installation has been fully completed and finalized.2.6 - Roof ArrayThe installation photos don't clearly show the quantity of PV modules installed in each array on the respective roof sections. Additionally, the visible configurations appear to differ from the layouts shown in both the plan set and the shade study. Please provide clearer and wider photos of each roof array and update the documentation as necessary to ensure consistency with the actual installation. 2.9 - Grounding Method for RackProvide a clear picture of the grounding method to the rack3.2 - AC DisconnectThe fuse rating value is not clearly visible in the provided photos. Please verify and confirm that the installed fuse is rated at 200 A, as specified in the approved SLD within the plan set.Please provide photographs of the blade disconnect switches installed between the PV system and the AC HUB, including clear identification of the 60 A busbar rating, as specified in the SLD. 4.1 - MSP Cover Open and 4.3 - MSP Dead Front RemovedEnsure the MSP breaker and rating is clearly visible. If needed, take a close up of the MSP Breaker.4.2 - MSP LabelPlease verify and confirm that the MSP busbar rating is 220 A, as specified in the SLD. 4.4 - MSP Solar BreakerThe SLD indicates two PV breaker panels: the main PV breaker panel with three breakers, and the PV surplus panel with two breakers. The photos currently only shows the PV surplus panel with the two breakers. Please provide the missing main PV breaker panel.Additionally, the panel currently shown includes two 25 A breakers. According to the approved SLD, one of the PV branches must be protected by a 20 A breaker based on the installed PV module and microinverter configuration. job_stage.name: Site Survey
job_stage.description: Your project has moved into the Site Survey stage. Surveys are typically only taking a few hours at most and are scheduled within a week.

job_stage.name: Design
job_stage.description: Congratulations! Your solar project has moved into the Design stage. This process may take 1-2 weeks because we want to take the amount of time necessary to provide you with a flawless installation.

job_stage.name: Permitting
job_stage.description: Congratulations! Your solar project has moved into the Permitting stage. Now that we have your approved design, we are going through your local building jurisdiction for permitting.

job_stage.name: Installation
job_stage.description: Congratulations! Your solar project has moved into the Installation stage. One of our team members will be reaching out to schedule your installation. Most installations take less than a full day to complete.

job_stage.name: Inspection
job_stage.description: Congratulations! Your solar has been installed. The utility company and local building jurisdiction will now come out for an inspection of your solar system.

job_stage.name: PTO
job_stage.description: Congratulations! Your project is almost complete. Now that your system has passed inspection, your utility company will give you the green light to turn your system on. To learn more about the process.
